body.statement:
Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/4)\).  If \(\mathrm{oeq:global\text{-}endpoint\text{-}response}\) is resolved affirmatively, the raw error is bounded by \(\mathfrak R_{H,n}\). At the selected resolutions, \(\sqrt{\ell_n/(n_\ast h_n^d)}=h_n^s\), \(k_n^s[1+\log(1/k_n)]\le Ch_n^s/\ell_n\), and \(\ell_n/[n_\ast(h_nk_n)^{d/2}]+\eta_n^2=o(h_n^s)\) because \(2r<s\). Hence constants \(C_0,C_1\), depending only on \(d,s,R,m,M,b,B,L\), and a threshold \(n_0\), allowed also to depend on the fixed \(\delta\), satisfy, for every \(n_\ast\ge n_0\), \(\mathfrak R_{H,n}\le r_{H,n}=C_1h_n^s\le m/2\) and
\[
 \inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal M_s}\mathbb P_{\mathbf P}(\mathcal B_n)\ge1-\delta.
\]
On \(\mathcal B_n\), Weyl's inequality gives \(\widetilde H_p(u)\succeq(m-r_{H,n})I_d\succeq(m/2)I_d\); hence \(\widehat H_p=\Pi_{m/4}(\widetilde H_p)=\widetilde H_p\) simultaneously, and
\[
 \max_{p\ne q}\lvert\widehat\gamma_{pq}-\gamma_{pq}\rvert\le w_n.
\]
Consequently, the everywhere-defined \(\Psi_n\) has size at most \(\delta\) over \(\gamma_{pq}\le0\) and power at least \(1-\delta\) over \(\gamma_{pq}\ge3w_n\).
body.justification: The theorem makes the two-resolution rate auditable, proves clipping is inactive on the coverage event, and propagates the unmodified population Hessians to a strict causal certificate.
body.gap: ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT proves pointwise map central limit theorems on a flat torus and failure of global weak convergence, while existing multivariate-rank results do not cover Hessians or an infimum eigenvalue margin.
body.consumer: Applied users of multivariate transport counterfactuals can certify a margin separated from zero with controlled familywise error across regimes.

obligation.what_is_open: The class-uniform probability bound for the raw Hessian event at radius \(\mathfrak R_{H,n}\).
obligation.obstruction: It depends on the unresolved endpoint-response OEQ. In addition, the frozen descriptions of the boundary wavelet projection and smoothing kernel do not state the approximation, kernel-envelope, derivative-envelope, or concentration bounds needed to derive the displayed finite-sample radius. Assuming the raw event would assume the theorem's crux.
obligation.attempted: Verified every rate substitution, the negligibility of both remainder terms under \(2r<s\), clipping inactivity, the inverse perturbation bound, Weyl propagation to the margin, and the exact test thresholds.
obligation.partial_result:
Conditional on a simultaneous raw Hessian event
\[
 \max_{p\in\mathcal A}\lVert\widetilde H_p-H_p\rVert_\infty\le r_{H,n}\le m/2,
\]
the remainder of the theorem is deterministic.  Weyl's inequality gives \(\widetilde H_p\succeq(m-r_{H,n})I_d\succeq(m/2)I_d\), so clipping at \(m/4\) is inactive.  The inverse identity gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \lVert\widehat H_q\widehat H_p^{-1}-H_qH_p^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\le \lVert\widehat H_q-H_q\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\lVert\widehat H_p^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 &\quad+\lVert H_q\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \lVert\widehat H_p^{-1}(H_p-\widehat H_p)H_p^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 &\le\left(\frac2m+\frac{2M}{m^2}\right)r_{H,n}=w_n.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Symmetrization is an operator-norm contraction.  Weyl's inequality followed by
\(\lvert\inf a-\inf b\rvert\le\sup\lvert a-b\rvert\) therefore yields
\[
 \max_{p\ne q}\lvert\widehat\gamma_{pq}-\gamma_{pq}\rvert\le w_n.
\]
On this event, \(\gamma_{pq}\le0\) implies \(\widehat\gamma_{pq}\le w_n\), whereas \(\gamma_{pq}\ge3w_n\) implies \(\widehat\gamma_{pq}\ge2w_n>w_n\); these are the claimed size and power implications.

For fixed \(\delta\), \(\ell_n\asymp\log n_\ast\).  From \(n_\ast h_n^{2s+d}=\ell_n\) and \(k_n=h_n\ell_n^{-2/s}\), direct substitution gives
\[
 \frac{\ell_n}{n_\ast(h_nk_n)^{d/2}}
 =h_n^{2s}\ell_n^{d/s}=o(h_n^s)
\]
and
\[
 \eta_n
 =h_n^{s-r}\ell_n^{-2(s-r)/s}
 +h_n^{s-r}\ell_n^{(d+2r)/s}
 +h_n^{2s-r}\ell_n^{2(d+r)/s}.
\]
Because \(s-2r>0\), every squared term on the last display is \(o(h_n^s)\).  Also
\[
 k_n^s\{1+\log(1/k_n)\}
 =h_n^s\ell_n^{-2}\{1+O(\ell_n)\}=O(h_n^s/\ell_n),
\qquad
 \sqrt{\frac{\ell_n}{n_\ast h_n^d}}=h_n^s.
\]
What remains unproved from the frozen primitives is the asserted probability bound for the raw Hessian event: the endpoint-response OEQ is unresolved, and the definitions of \(Q_{k_n}\) and \(K_{h_n}\) do not state the approximation, operator-envelope, derivative-envelope, or concentration inequalities needed to derive \(\mathfrak R_{H,n}\).
